# Quantum Erasure Recovery Compiler

> Exact minimum post-erasure CNOT cost for extracting one unknown stabilizer-encoded qubit onto a prescribed hardware site.

## Read the science

- [Overview](README.md) gives the result, architecture comparison and reading routes.
- [Model](science/model.md) defines the channel, flagged loss and charged resources.
- [Compiler and converse](science/theorem.md) derive the minimum T-join, one CNOT per selected edge and adaptive branch converse.
- [Complexity](science/complexity.md) separates polynomial routing per pair from NP-complete representative selection.
- [Benchmarks](science/benchmarks.md) cover the five-qubit code, Steane code and generalized Smolin witness.
- [Related work](science/related-work.md) and [bibliography](references/bibliography.bib) record primary comparisons.

## Study and verify

- [Gottesman bridge](learning/GOTTESMAN_BRIDGE.md) gives source sections and notation transfer.
- [Milestones](learning/MILESTONES.md) give the common learning route.
- [Worked example](learning/WORKED_EXAMPLE.md) connects one CNOT, measurement signs and graph cost.
- [Verification](verification/README.md) gives the reference compiler, input format and reproduction commands.

The general theorem assumes ideal single-qubit stabilizer controls, free classical feedforward and post-erasure CNOTs on a known graph. The Smolin-family witness gives a separate lower bound against arbitrary two-site gates. Compilation time, depth and fault tolerance have different resource definitions.
